title: The board that was typed by hand

terminal.description: The route board runs in the Browser panel and reloads every time you save. This shell is in your workspace if you want to look around.

tasks.title: Draw the board from the data
tasks.description:
Write `renderBoard(list, routes)` in `src/board.js`. It fills `list` (the `<ul id="route-list">`) with one item per route, in the order of the array, and nothing else.

Each item is an `<li class="route">` with:

- a `data-id` attribute set to the route's `id`
- an element with the class `route-name` holding the name as plain text
- the hold colour and the setter's name somewhere in the item, for example `Blue holds, set by Hollis`

Build the elements with `document.createElement` and put text in with `textContent`. A name like `Jump <Start>` must show exactly like that.

The check swaps `src/routes.js` for a file with routes of its own, so keep exporting `routes` from it.
nextSteps: Open `src/routes.js` and look at the shape of one route.
In `renderBoard`, create one `<li>` for a single route and append it to `list`.
Turn that into a loop over every route, and clear the list first so the hand-typed items go.
Add the name, colour and setter with `textContent`, then save and look at the Browser panel.
hints: The hand-typed items in `index.html` show the markup one route should have. Your job is to build that same markup from an object.
`document.createElement('li')` gives you an element that is not on the page yet. Set its class, `dataset.id` and children, then `append` it to the list.
Clear the list with `list.replaceChildren()` before adding items, and set every piece of text with `textContent`, never `innerHTML`, so `<Start>` stays text.

tasks.title: Grade badges at a glance
tasks.description:
Give every route item a grade badge: an element with the class `grade` whose text is the grade, such as `V4`.

The badge also gets a class for its band, so the stylesheet can colour it:

- `grade-easy` for `V0` to `V2`
- `grade-mid` for `V3` to `V5`
- `grade-hard` for `V6` and up, including two-digit grades like `V10`

So a `V4` badge has the classes `grade grade-mid`.
nextSteps: Write a small function that takes a grade like `'V4'` and returns `'easy'`, `'mid'` or `'hard'`.
Create a `<span>` for the badge in each route item and set its text to the grade.
Add the `grade` class and the band class to it.
Save and check that the badges on the board change colour.
hints: The grade is a string. The band depends on the number after the `V`.
`'V10'.slice(1)` is `'10'`, and `Number()` turns that into a number you can compare.
Compare the number with 2 and 5 to pick the band, then set `className` to `grade grade-` followed by it.

tasks.title: An empty wall says so
tasks.description:
On reset days every route comes down and the routes array is empty. The board should then say so instead of showing a blank box. In `src/main.js`: - when `routes` is empty, `#route-list` has no items and the `

` line is visible - when there are routes, `#board-empty` stays hidden `#board-empty` starts with the `hidden` attribute in `index.html`.
nextSteps: Find `#board-empty` in `index.html` and notice its `hidden` attribute.
Set whether it is hidden from the length of `routes`.
Try it: empty the array in `src/routes.js` for a moment, save, and look at the board. Put the routes back after.
hints: Elements have a `hidden` property that mirrors the attribute. You can set it to `true` or `false`.
If the list still shows the hand-typed routes with no data, `renderBoard` is not clearing the list before it adds items.
One line does it: hidden should be true exactly when `routes.length` is greater than 0.
